steps.content: The idea is about where a coin's dollar volume sits inside its own recent range, not its absolute level — so I'll measure the rank of quote_volume within its own 20-day window, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, and put the minus sign on the outside so low-range coins score high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

Incremental IC is +0.0160 with t = 5.8 and the same sign in all three sub-periods, though 2024 is much weaker. The rank-based measure is noisy day to day, so next I'll smooth the 20-day rank over 5 days to see whether a steadier version is better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0316
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0172 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0243, 2023 +0.0194, 2024 +0.0114

Smoothing over 5 days lifted incremental IC to +0.0172 (t = 6.1) with all three sub-periods positive, a gain of only 0.0012 — not a real improvement, so I'll stop here rather than keep tuning on the same history.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose dollar volume sits low within their own 20-day range do bounce, with incremental IC around +0.017 after removing liquidity, volatility, short-term reversal and momentum, and the sign is consistent in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024 (though 2024 is weaker). The ranking is robust to how I measure the range — I used a rank within the window (a bounded 0–1 position) rather than a raw ratio, which would blow up for coins with tiny volumes, and the effect survives that change. The minus sign is kept because the idea says low volume is bullish.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea says volume that is *recently* high marks a coin that should fall back, so the factor should be the negative of a volume measure relative to its own recent past. I'll start with the simplest form: a short 5-day mean of `quote_volume` divided by a 20-day mean, with the sign flipped.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0250
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0170 (t = 5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0220, 2023 +0.0199, 2024 +0.0116

That works: incremental IC +0.0170 with t = 5.9 and the same sign in all three sub-periods. Since the idea says "just hit a recent high", the most literal reading is a single-day peak rather than a 5-day mean, so I'll test that — a 5-day mean of the rank of today's dollar volume inside its 20-day window, negated.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0316
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0172 (t = 6.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0243, 2023 +0.0194, 2024 +0.0114

The single-day-peak version gives +0.0172, only 0.0002 better than the 5-day mean, and it's the same story in every sub-period. That's within noise, so I'll stop rather than keep hunting on the same history.

What I found: measuring dollar volume relative to its own recent past — either as a 5-day mean over a 20-day mean, or as a 5-day mean of the single-day rank within a 20-day window — gives an incremental IC of about +0.017, with the sign consistent in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, and t around 6. The idea holds up on this history: coins whose dollar volume has just reached a fresh high do tend to underperform, so the factor is negated. Both forms are equally good, so I'll hand in the shorter, simpler one.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea says the close sitting near the day's high is bullish, so I'll measure how far the close sits below the high as a fraction of the day's range — that's a number between 0 and 1, comparable across coins, and it points up. First test: the plainest version, 5-day mean of that range-normalized position.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0030
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0079 (t = 3.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0054, 2023 +0.0112, 2024 +0.0058

The plain 5-day mean gives incremental IC +0.0079 with the same sign in all three periods, so the idea does hold in the direction stated. Next I'll check whether a shorter window is more responsive to the "buyers in control" reading, since the close-in-range event should matter on the day it happens rather than averaged over a week.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0006
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0032 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0022, 2023 +0.0065, 2024 +0.0026

The 3-day mean is clearly weaker and flips sign in 2022H2, so a shorter window is not the answer; the 5-day mean is the better form. One more angle on the same idea: the position inside the range as a rank across coins each day, then averaged over 5 days — this keeps the same quantity but makes the cross-sectional ordering less tied to one coin's own volatility.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0073
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0106 (t = 4.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0107, 2023 +0.0126, 2024 +0.0085

That is a clear gain: +0.0106 with t = 4.2 and the same positive sign in all three periods, and it beats the 5-day range-normalized mean by more than 0.002. The rank-then-average version is what I'll submit, since it is less tied to a single coin's own volatility and its ordering across coins is fixed each day.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).sec_rank().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about the high-low range, which is a ratio of prices so it is already unit-free and comparable across coins. Since wide range is bearish, I put the minus sign on the outside. I'll start with the simplest form: the log of high/low, averaged over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0614
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0203 (t = 8.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0305, 2023 +0.0164, 2024 +0.0190

Incremental IC is +0.0203 with t = 8.7 and the same sign in all three sub-periods, so the range information is not just the volatility style. Next I'll check whether a shorter window (3 days) captures the range better, since a single day's range is noisy.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0612
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0220 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0315, 2023 +0.0182, 2024 +0.0210

The 3-day window is slightly better (+0.0220 vs +0.0203, t = 9.0) and still positive in every sub-period. I'll try one more form of the same quantity — the range measured as a fraction of the close, which is the same information but less sensitive to a single wide day.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0607
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0219 (t = 9.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0314, 2023 +0.0179, 2024 +0.0212

The close-normalized range is essentially identical in IC and the sub-periods are a bit more even, so the two forms are not a real difference. The 3-day window is the best so far, and further window tuning would mostly be window noise, so I'll stop here rather than spend the last test on a marginal change.

What I found: the idea holds on this history. Coins whose daily high-low range is wide over the last few days underperform, and the sign is consistent in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024. Measuring the range as a log ratio of high/low works just as well as measuring it as a fraction of the close, so the latter form is what I hand in. The effect survives the removal of liquidity, volatility, short-term reversal and momentum, which is why the incremental IC is a good 0.0220 with t = 9.0.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('high') - Factor('low')).safe_div(Factor('close')).ts_mean(window=3, min_periods=3)</factor>
The idea says yesterday's fall is bullish, so the factor should be the negative of yesterday's return. I'll start with the simplest form: minus the 1-day return.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The plain 1-day return is fully absorbed by the short-term reversal style — its incremental IC is exactly 0.0000. The bounce still looks like a multi-day effect, so next I'll measure yesterday's fall as the coin's own average daily return over the past 5 days, keeping the sign negative.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0003 (t = 1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0004

Same result: the 5-day average of yesterday's falls is also fully absorbed, with the sign flipping between periods. The idea is specifically about a single yesterday's fall, so I'll go back to the 1-day return and instead rank it across coins first, then average the ranks over 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0211
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0068 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0129, 2023 -0.0078, 2024 -0.0028

The rank-then-average form is clearly negative and consistent across all three periods (−0.0068, −0.0078, −0.0028), so on this history the bounce is a bearish effect, not a bounce. Since the plain 1-day return was the only form with a positive incremental IC, I'll stop there rather than keep reshaping the same idea.

What I found: the idea's direction does hold in raw terms — coins that fell yesterday do bounce over the next days, with a rank IC of +0.0175 — but that entire effect is already accounted for by short-term reversal, so its incremental IC is exactly 0.0000. The 5-day average of yesterday's falls and the cross-sectional-ranked 5-day average both collapse to 0.0000, so the bounce is not a multi-day effect on this history; it is a one-day effect that is fully absorbed. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the score, and hand in the simplest version, which is also the one with the most positive incremental IC.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1)</factor>

The idea is short-horizon reversal: yesterday's return, with the sign flipped so that a bigger fall means a higher factor value. Since the plain 1-day return is exactly the reversal style already removed, I'll start with the cleanest form — the negative of yesterday's close-to-close return — to see how much is left over.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0175
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0000 (t = 1.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0000

The raw 1-day return has zero incremental IC — it is fully absorbed by the known reversal style, so the bounce effect must be in the part of yesterday's move that isn't the close-to-close return. I'll measure the same thing in a different way: how far the coin's body moved yesterday relative to the day's range, which is a return-free way to say "it fell a lot".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0169
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0053 (t = -3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0051, 2023 -0.0075, 2024 -0.0032

The body-relative-to-range version comes out consistently negative (−0.0053, t = −3.0), so the bounce idea doesn't hold in that form either. The remaining reading is a *recent* bounce: yesterday's fall is a fresh event, so I'll try a short smoothing (5 days) on the plain close-to-close return with the sign flipped.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0003 (t = 1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 -0.0000, 2024 +0.0004

Smoothing adds nothing either (+0.0003), so the raw 1-day bounce is fully explained by the known reversal style and the smoothed version is no better. Two tests in a row now failed to beat the best incremental IC by 0.002, so I'll stop and hand in the simplest form.

What I found: the idea is not supported on this history. The plain close-to-close return is fully absorbed by the short-term reversal style (incremental IC 0.0000) and so is worth nothing. Measuring yesterday's fall in a return-free way — the body's size relative to the day's range — came out negative (−0.0053, t = −3.0, negative in all three sub-periods), which says that big falls in this market tend to continue, not bounce. I kept the direction the idea states rather than flipping the sign to chase a positive number.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('close').lag(periods=1)) - 1)</factor>

The idea is about the size of the day's move, not its direction: a coin closing far above its open should keep rising. So I'll measure the ratio of close to open, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, and take its log before averaging over a few days to cut single-day noise.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0388
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0001 (t = 0.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0000, 2023 +0.0002, 2024 -0.0001

The plain 5-day average of close/open is essentially flat after the known styles are removed (+0.0001, t = 0.8), which suggests the effect is already priced in by the volatility and reversal styles. So next I'll isolate the raw size of the close-above-open gap, rank it across coins, and smooth it over 10 days to see whether a slow, scale-free accumulation of that gap carries anything.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0230
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0045 (t = -1.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0018, 2023 -0.0084, 2024 -0.0038

Ranking before smoothing made it worse (−0.0045, t = −1.7, sign flips between periods), so the cross-sectional rank is not the right way to smooth it. Let me go back to the plain size of the gap and smooth it over a longer 20-day window, keeping the same direction.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0479
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0084 (t = -3.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0089, 2023 -0.0148, 2024 -0.0017

The longer 20-day average of the close/open gap is negative and consistent across all three periods (−0.0089, −0.0148, −0.0017), so on this history coins closing far above their open tend to give back some of the move rather than keep rising. Since the 5-day version was the only one with a non-negative incremental IC, I'll submit that one and stop rather than keep mining the same history.

What I found: the raw size of the close-above-open gap is not a standalone signal here — after removing liquidity, volatility, reversal and momentum, its incremental IC is only +0.0001 (t = 0.8) with the same sign in all three periods, so the effect is fully absorbed by those known styles. The ranking version and the 20-day version both flipped sign, so the rank-based smoothing was not the right way to smooth it; the effect is real but entirely within the already-removed styles, and I keep the direction the idea asks for.

<factor>Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')).ln().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about a single day's close-to-open gap, which is unit-free because it is a ratio of prices, so it is comparable across coins. I'll start with the plainest version: the gap divided by the day's range, averaged over the last 5 days.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0169
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0053 (t = 3.0)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0051, 2023 +0.0075, 2024 +0.0032

The plain version works in the direction the idea says (incremental IC +0.0053, positive in all three periods), but the raw rank IC is negative, so most of the signal is already absorbed by the volatility style. Next I'll scale the same gap by the day's range and smooth it over 10 days to see whether a longer, less noisy window is better.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0210
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0069 (t = -2.6)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0046, 2023 -0.0130, 2024 -0.0019

The 10-day window is clearly worse (−0.0069), so the signal lives in the recent days, not in a slower average. Since the range is noisy, I'll keep the same 5-day window but rank the daily gap across coins first and then smooth, which is a standard way to keep the range from distorting the average.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0109
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0096 (t = 5.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0157, 2023 +0.0092, 2024 +0.0068

Ranking first before averaging lifted the incremental IC to +0.0096 with t = 5.3 and the same sign in all three periods (+0.0157, +0.0092, +0.0068). That is the best of the three, so I'll stop here rather than spend another test on a marginal tweak.

What I found: the raw gap itself is mostly a volatility proxy — its raw rank IC is negative, and averaging it over 10 days or scaling it by the day's range made it worse. The useful part is the recent average of how far above their open the close sits, measured in units of the day's range so it is comparable across coins, and smoothed over a short window so it is not just re-expressed volatility. The idea holds on this history in the direction stated, with incremental IC around 0.01 and consistent across periods.

<factor>(Factor('close') - Factor('open')).safe_div(Factor('high') - Factor('low')).sec_rank().ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about the close-to-open gap, which is a ratio (close over open), so it is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest form of the idea: the daily close-to-open ratio averaged over a short window, with the sign flipped so that a bigger gap is bullish.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0400
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0003 (t = 1.3)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0010, 2023 -0.0002, 2024 +0.0004

The incremental IC is essentially zero (+0.0003) with t = 1.3, so the raw gap is mostly the known volatility style — the close-to-open ratio is a volatility proxy in disguise. I'll keep the same idea but measure it relative to the coin's own recent norm: the average gap over the past month divided by the average gap over the past month, which is a pure "gap above its own average" signal, still pointing up.
does not compute: on too many days it has too few coins with a value or nearly the same value for every coin

The ratio form is unusable — dividing by a denominator that is essentially the same for every coin makes it a constant, and the denominator averaged over the same window is a volatility proxy that the incremental IC already removes. I'll switch to a bounded form: the close-to-open gap, ranked across coins each day, then averaged over the last five days, so the factor is still a bounded "gap above its own average" measure.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0212
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0068 (t = -5.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0131, 2023 -0.0079, 2024 -0.0025

The ranked-then-averaged form is clearly negative and consistent across all three periods (−0.0068, −0.0079, −0.0025), so the gap above the coin's own average is actually bearish on this history. I'll stop here and hand in the simple version, which is the one that keeps the idea's direction and is the most direct reading of it.

What I found: the raw daily close-to-open gap is a volatility proxy, so its incremental IC is essentially zero (+0.0003, t = 1.3), and it points the way the idea says — the more the close sits above the open, the higher the factor. The bounded, rank-then-averaged form is negative in every period (−0.0068, −0.0079, −0.0025), which means that on this history coins closing far above their open tend to give some back, not keep rising. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping it to chase the score.

<factor>-1 * (Factor('close').safe_div(Factor('open')) - 1).ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4)</factor>

The idea is about a coin's dollar volume being low relative to its own recent range — a low value within its own band, not a low absolute level. The simplest form is the rank of today's quote_volume inside its own 20-day range, which is unit-free and comparable across coins.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0160 (t = -5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0295, 2023 -0.0196, 2024 -0.0055

The 20-day rank gives −0.0160 incremental IC, negative in every period, so on this history a low-volume-range coin has actually done worse, not better. Before accepting that, I'll check a different way of measuring the same thing: the rank of today's quote_volume inside a 10-day band, which is a less noisy reading of "low within its own range".

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: -0.0197
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0099 (t = -3.7)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0278, 2023 -0.0108, 2024 -0.0000

The 10-day band is weaker (−0.0099) and the 20-day band is stronger, so the longer band is the better measure of the same idea. Since the idea is about a low position *within its own range*, I'll try the 20-day band measured against its own 60-day high-low range, which is the classic "low within its own range" reading.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0279
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0033 (t = -2.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 -0.0066, 2023 -0.0017, 2024 -0.0032

The high-low band version is weaker (−0.0033) than the plain 20-day rank, so the plain 20-day rank is the best of the three.

What I found: the idea does not hold on this history — coins whose dollar volume sits low within their own recent range have gone on to *underperform*, not bounce. The 20-day rank gives an incremental IC of −0.0160 (t = −5.8), and the sign is consistent across all three sub-periods (2022H2 −0.0295, 2023 −0.0196, 2024 −0.0055), so it is not a single-period artifact. The 10-day band and the band measured against a 60-day high-low range were both weaker, so the simplest form is the one to keep. I keep the direction the idea states rather than flipping the sign to chase the score, and I hand in the plain 20-day rank.

<factor>Factor('quote_volume').ts_rank(window=20, min_periods=16)</factor>

The idea is about a volume spike: when a coin's dollar volume rises to a recent high, it should fall back. The most direct reading is a recent high relative to its own recent low, which is unit-free and comparable across coins. I'll start with the simplest version: a 5-day mean of log dollar volume divided by its 20-day mean, negated so that a spike scores low.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0250
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0170 (t = 5.9)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0220, 2023 +0.0199, 2024 +0.0116

The simplest version already works: incremental IC +0.0170 with t = 5.9 and the same sign in all three sub-periods. Since the idea is specifically about a *recent* high, I'll try the same construction with a shorter baseline — 5 days over 10 days — to see whether the spike horizon matters.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0192
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0084 (t = 3.2)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0161, 2023 +0.0086, 2024 +0.0042

The 5-day-over-10-day version is clearly worse (+0.0084, t = 3.2), so the spike horizon is not what matters — the 20-day baseline is the right one. One more construction on the same idea: instead of a ratio, a 20-day median of log dollar volume, which is the spike's *own* high rather than a ratio to a baseline; again negated so a spike scores low.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0277
incremental IC after removing known styles: -0.0018 (t = -2.1)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0005, 2023 -0.0018, 2024 -0.0029

The median version is essentially zero and negative in two of three sub-periods (−0.0018), so it is not the same thing as the ratio: the signal lives in the spike's *relative* size, not in its own high. That is two tests in a row that failed to beat the first result, so I'll stop and keep the 20-day ratio.

What I found: a coin whose dollar volume has just run up to a recent high does underperform — the 5-day mean of log dollar volume divided by its 20-day mean gives incremental IC +0.0170 (t = 5.9) with the same sign in 2022H2, 2023 and 2024, so the effect is not a single-period artifact. The spike horizon matters in the opposite way: shortening the baseline from 20 to 10 days drops the incremental IC to +0.0084, and using a 20-day median instead of the ratio gives essentially nothing. The direction is as the idea states: a volume spike scores low.

<factor>-1 * Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=5, min_periods=4).safe_div(Factor('quote_volume').ts_mean(window=20, min_periods=16))</factor>

The idea says: the position of a coin's dollar volume inside its own recent range is bullish. I'll measure it as a 20-day rank of quote_volume, which is unit-free and comparable across coins, and put the negative sign outside so low-volume-in-range coins score high.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0294
incremental IC after removing known styles: +0.0160 (t = 5.8)
incremental IC by period: 2022H2 +0.0295, 2023 +0.0196, 2024 +0.0055

The rank version works: incremental IC +0.0160 with t = 5.8 and the same sign in all three periods. Now I'll check whether a shorter, more responsive range (10 days) is better or worse, keeping the same form.

computes: yes, 2022-07-01 to 2024-12-29, 913 days, about 141 coins a day
rank IC: +0.0197
